title: The Koras-Russell cylinder as an affine modification of A^4: a commuting square through a motivic 4-sphere and a one-point Borel-Moore defect
description:
A global dissection of the Dubouloz–Moser-Jauslin–Poloni locally nilpotent derivation on the Koras–Russell cylinder X × A1, and the geometry underneath it.

The kernel is a polynomial ring in three variables; the derivation has no slice, exactly and with no degree bound; its plinth ideal is not principal, and a known subideal already encloses its zero locus in a union of two loci, one divisorial and one of codimension two; the quotient morphism is neither surjective nor equidimensional; and after inverting one explicit function the cylinder is a trivial A1-bundle over A3. Read as gluing data, this presents the cylinder as a canonical affine modification of A4 whose centre has a component singular along a line, so it cannot be carried to any smooth centre by an automorphism of A4. The two modification steps commute: one order runs through the singular cylinder over the auxiliary threefold, the other through a smooth fourfold identified with the member Q_{(3,1),z^2-1/4} of the Asok–Dubouloz–Østvær family, a model of the motivic 4-sphere. A four-corner motivic ledger shows the smooth route creating an L2 packet at one arrow and removing it at the other, with the removing arrow's exceptional locus empty over exactly one point of its centre. Finally, at integral Borel–Moore level, H^BM_4(Y_1;Z) is infinite cyclic, generated by the fundamental class of either component of the doubled fibre over the origin; the generator is supported on the modification divisor, and the inverse image of its representative is the same plane with the fibre over the defect point deleted, whose own fundamental class vanishes in the contractible source; dually, and with no properness hypothesis, the cohomological pullback of the Poincaré dual vanishes. The defect therefore accounts exactly for the Euler and Grothendieck-class change and locates its cycle-level content at one named point.

Nothing here bears on whether X × A1 is isomorphic to A4. Every computational claim is machine-certified in exact arithmetic and reproducible from this repository with a single command: 883 checks, 713 PASS, 0 FAIL, 22 frozen ledgers replaying identically.
